problem: Existing embodied referring-expression and QA tasks (ERE, EQA, VLN) only involve navigation and linguistic interaction; they do not require the agent to physically manipulate objects (open, move, pick up) to reveal the information needed to answer a question.
motivation: Real robots must navigate, localize a target among many similar objects (e.g., several drawers) via referring expressions, and manipulate occluding objects to answer questions. No existing task combines vision, language, navigation and manipulation, so the authors define a task and benchmark that do.
key_idea: Introduce Remote Embodied Manipulation Question Answering (REMQA) and a modular baseline: semantic-map-prior navigation, MAttNet-style LAN referring expression comprehension, manipulation-type classification, and a CNN-LSTM QA module over before/after-manipulation frames.
insight: Interaction matters: the EQA baseline without manipulation scores far below IQA and the proposed model (SQA 0.330 vs 0.540 on existence, 0.131 vs 0.284 on spatial). Navigation gains come mainly from privileged 3D semantic memory built from simulator metadata, and the modular REC design outperforms a BiLSTM baseline (66.57/70.45 vs 70.27/74.12 with LAN+MaskRCNN), showing the value of decomposing expressions.
method: Navigation: agent pre-explores each scene along sampling paths to build a 3D voxel semantic memory from simulator metadata, projects it to a 2D semantic map, looks up the target label and plans the shortest path with the Floyd algorithm.

Referring Expression Comprehension: Language Attention Network (from MAttNet) splits the expression into subject, location and relationship modules, computes weighted matching scores against detectron2 detections.

Manipulation: a classifier picks Open/Move/Pickup from the target's semantic label; the arm moves to the target using 3D memory, and manipulation is auto-executed for objects within the end-effector sphere (no action generation or dynamic planning).
Question Answering: CNN encodes I_start and I_end, a 2-layer LSTM encodes the question, image-question attention fuses the features, and a softmax classifier predicts the answer.

Data generation: 10k+ images sampled by BFS from AI2-THOR to pretrain segmentation and REC; scene graphs (distance and 3D IoU relations) generate template referring expressions and the questions (existence, counting, spatial).
REMQA dataset: 120 scenes (100 train / 20 test), 4072 questions, 60 object types, each scene with multiple configurations giving different answers.

setting.backbone: CNN-LSTM QA, LAN + detectron2 REC (trained); navigation is a semantic-map planner (not learned)
setting.training_data: Self-generated data in AI2-THOR: 10k+ sampled images with auto annotations, template referring expressions, and REMQA train split (100 scenes)
setting.observation: Egocentric RGB-D with simulator metadata, agent location and arm configuration
setting.action_space: Grid navigation along planned shortest path; arm movement with automatic Open/Move/Pickup
setting.privileged: Pre-exploration to build 3D semantic memory/2D semantic map from simulator metadata; automatic manipulation execution within end sphere

results: The framework beats EQA and IQA baselines in most QA metrics (e.g., S_QA 0.540 vs 0.488 existence for IQA, 0.284 vs 0.216 spatial), losing to IQA on S_N and S_L for counting. Navigation with the semantic map reaches SR 0.729 versus 0.396 for SAVN at 50 steps.
limitations: Navigation relies on a pre-built semantic map from simulator metadata, and only covers previously seen scenes, limiting generalization
Manipulation is auto-executed within the end-effector sphere, with no real action generation or planning
Only simulated, template-generated questions with three question types; no real-robot validation
